newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm in technical bounce.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm in technical bounce.

text.p: Chilean shares closed firm in a technical rally with most buy orders from traders dealing their own portfolios, said brokers.
The bullish mood is expected to continue at the opening, although the market remains range-bound with the blue chip IPSA index fluctuating between 96.5 and 100 points.
"We will keep seeing lateral movements like this as there's no structural change in the bolsa," said one trader.
The IPSA index ended up 0.81 percent at 97.84 points. The general IGPA index gained 0.2 percent at 5,304.91 points.
Turnover rose to 10.8 billion pesos from 8.6 billion pesos Monday.
Traders said the market was hesitant ahead of Wednesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, even though most analysts agree the Fed will leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
Commodity stocks were among the leaders with investors snapping up bargains after recent sharp falls in forestry shares and steel-maker Cap, said dealers.
Cap, which has lost ground recently on jitters over steel prices, climbed 2.8 percent to 1,100 pesos.
Chile's largest wood pulp producer Copec gained 1.84 percent to 1,660 pesos, with paper-maker CMPC up 0.59 percent at 5,130 pesos.
Losers were mainly lightly traded stocks with financial holding company Cruz Blanca down 3.45 percent at 168 pesos and fishing firm Itata off 2.83 percent at 103 pesos.
